title: 自維連立合意1年 関係深化は途上
body:
自民党と日本維新の会が連立政権合意書を交わして２０日で１年となる。５割超の項目で達成のメドがついたが、維新は残る項目について早期実現を自民に迫っている。連立合意以外の課題も山積しており、２年目に入る連立はどこまで関係を深化させられるかが問われそうだ。（三歩一真希）【表】一目でわかる…維新の現状と課題
「想定しなかった課題も出てくる。連立合意の更新は必要になる」。維新の柴田幹事長は１９日、連立合意の実現を重視する姿勢を記者団に強調した。
自民と維新の連立合意書は、数値目標や達成時期を多く掲げたことが特徴だ。吉村代表（大阪府知事）は「何を進めるか明らかにしたのが自公（連立）政権との大きな違いだ」と指摘する。維新によると、「副首都構想」関連法の成立や国家情報局の設置など全６３項目のうち５７％にあたる３６項目で達成か、その見込みがついたという。
ただ、維新が重視する社会保障改革や衆院議員定数削減などについては、実現が遅れている。維新は連立合意書を更新して重要法案の成立期限の明記などを求めるが、自民は「政権運営の自由度を縛りかねない」（幹部）として現行の連立合意書を当面維持すべきだと主張している。
維新は、規制改革の推進も本格化させたい考えだ。９月の内閣改造で中司宏・前幹事長が規制改革相として入閣したのに合わせ、党にも調査会を新たに設置した。自動運転の実現や公務員制度改革などを目指すが、業界団体を支持基盤に抱える自民には急進的な改革に拒否感が根強い。
政策以外にも課題が残る。維新の本拠地・大阪では、これまで自民、維新両党の候補者が衆院選小選挙区で競合してきた。このため、４月に次期衆院選に向けた候補者調整を幹事長レベルで進めることを確認したが、その後は目立った動きが見られない。吉村氏は来春の統一地方選に合わせ、大阪都構想の是非を問う３度目の住民投票を実施する準備を進めているが、自民は同時実施に否定的だ。

title: H3の10号機 火星圏の物質採取へ
body:
日本の主力ロケット「H3」の10号機が20日（火）午前4時41分、鹿児島県の種子島宇宙センターから打ち上げられ、搭載した火星衛星探査機「MMX」を予定の軌道に投入し、打ち上げは成功しました。▼【写真で見る】H3ロケット10号機　打ち上げの迫力MMXは火星の衛星「フォボス」で砂や岩石などを採取し、2031年に地球に持ち帰る計画で、世界初となる火星圏からのサンプルリターンを目指します。
H3ロケット10号機は、20日（火）午前4時41分03秒に打ち上げられました。MMXは打ち上げからおよそ1時間11分後にロケットから分離され、地球から火星へ向かう「火星遷移軌道」に投入されました。
MMXはJAXA＝宇宙航空研究開発機構が主導する探査計画です。およそ1年かけて2027年に火星圏に到達し、火星のまわりを回る2つの衛星のうち、火星に近い「フォボス」を詳しく調べます。フォボスは、地球にとっての月にあたる天体で、いびつな形をしています。MMXは地形や表面の物質などを観測して着陸地点を選び、2回の着陸で合わせて10グラム以上の砂や岩石などを採取する計画です。もう一つの衛星「ダイモス」や火星の大気なども観測し、2030年に火星圏を離れます。採取したサンプルはカプセルに収め、打ち上げから5年後の2031年に地球へ持ち帰る予定です。実現すれば、探査機が火星圏で採取した物質を地球に持ち帰る、世界初の「サンプルリターン」となります。
大きな目的の一つは、火星の衛星がどのように誕生したのかを解明することです。フォボスやダイモスの起源をめぐっては、飛来した小惑星が火星の重力に捕らえられたとする説と、火星に大きな天体が衝突し、飛び散った物質が集まってできたとする説があり、決着はついていません。MMXは現地での観測と、地球に持ち帰ったサンプルの分析を組み合わせ、この謎に迫ります。また、フォボスには、隕石の衝突によって火星から飛び出した物質が降り積もっていると考えられています。採取したサンプルにこうした物質が含まれていれば、火星の環境がどのように変化してきたのかを調べる手がかりになると期待されています。MMXは、小惑星探査機「はやぶさ」「はやぶさ2」で培った探査やサンプル採取の技術を生かす計画です。火星圏と地球を往復する技術や、衛星への着陸・試料採取の技術を獲得し、将来の惑星・衛星探査につなげる狙いもあります。

title: 上皇后さま92歳に 穏やかな日々
body: 上皇后美智子さまが、きょう（20日）、92歳の誕生日を迎えられました。宮内庁はきょう（20日）、上皇ご夫妻がお住まいの仙洞御所内にある談話室で和やかに会話される写真などを公開しました（今月6日撮影）。【きょう公開】上皇さまと談笑される上皇后美智子さま【写真を見る】■この1年の体調側近は、上皇后さまの体調について「高齢に伴うご体力の低下により、以前に比べてお疲れやすくなることが多く、ご散策時にお歩きになる距離も次第に短くなっていらっしゃいます」と明かしました。午後に微熱が出る症状が続くほか、心不全の診断指標「BNP値」は正常値を超えているということですが、体調自体に大きな変化はないということで、「陛下と静かで穏やかな日々をお過ごし」としています。また、2022年に診断された「深部静脈血栓症」が再発しないよう、上皇さまとともに御用地内の散策や筋力低下防止の軽い運動を続けられています。■生活や“お届け物”1月には、新年一般参賀に出席されました。5月には、神奈川県葉山町の御用邸で静養。上皇さまと手をつないで近くの岬を散策し、地元住民らとの交流を楽しまれました。猛暑や体調などを理由に取りやめとなった予定もありましたが、一年を通して元気な姿を見せられました。また、過去に交流があった人たちからは今も本や機関誌などが多数届けられ、御所内の部屋で大切に保管されているといいます。去年末には、石川県立津幡高校の生徒たちが、繭を使って伝統の絹織物「牛首紬」を作り、仙洞御所に送りました。生徒の活動は、上皇后さまが長年続けてきた養蚕から着想を得たものだということで、受け取った上皇后さまは驚くとともに、生徒たちの取り組みに感心されていたということです。このほか、普段の生活ではテレビや側近との会話を通して社会の出来事に触れているほか、夜には音楽番組やバレーボールなどスポーツの国際試合をご覧になることもあるといいます。また、両陛下や皇族方が海外訪問や誕生日の時などに仙洞御所を訪問されることを楽しみにされているということです。

title: スイミングスクール 80代溺れ搬送
body: 北海道旭川市のスイミングスクールのプールで10月19日、高齢の女性が溺れているのが見つかり、病院に搬送されました。警察が当時の状況を調べています。19日午後2時ごろ、旭川市永山のスイミングスクールから「高齢女性がプールで溺れた」などと、消防に通報がありました。消防などによりますと、女性は80代のレッスン生で、意識がもうろうとし、会話ができない状態で病院に搬送されました。当時、レッスンが終了し、仲間2人がプール内で遊泳中、女性が溺れているのを発見したということです。プール付近に監視員がいたかなどは分かっておらず、警察が女性が溺れた状況などを調べています。

title: 増える訪日客 ポイ捨て被害深刻
body:
コロナ禍の終息から３年。インバウンド（訪日外国人客）の回復も一因となり、観光地や繁華街でごみのポイ捨て被害が深刻さを増している。東京都は違反者に過料を科す条例の制定に向けた議論を本格化させた。実際に徴収が始まれば、都道府県では初の試みとなる。都が規制強化にかじを切った背景を探った。（五十川由夏）【写真】渋谷センター街でポイ捨てや路上喫煙に目を光らせる指導員ら
９月２４日早朝、５連休を終えて人影が消えた新宿・歌舞伎町は、さながら「ごみの街」のようだった。
飲食店前に置かれた事業系ごみの上に、酒の缶や瓶、飲食物の空き容器が投げ捨てられて積み重なり、カラスが群がる。人目につかないビルの隙間にもごみが押し込まれ、路上には壊れたビニール傘が無造作に捨てられていた。
新宿区が２０２５年度に繁華街の路上から回収したのは１６４トンで、１９年度から２６トン増えた。区が２５年度に家庭などから集めたごみ（約６万４０００トン）と比べると少ないものの、分別されていないため収集に手間がかかる。日本人に交じって捨てていく外国人の姿もあり、地元商店街の杉山元茂理事長（７３）は「夜になると、ごみが湧くように増える」と嘆く。
問題は繁華街だけにとどまらない。埼玉、山梨両県に接する奥多摩町ではコロナ禍以来、河原のバーベキューごみが目立つ。アジア系外国人らの間で「密」を避ける場所としてＳＮＳを通じて広まったとみられ、町観光産業課の大串清文課長は「町だけで対応するのは難しい」と明かす。
小池百合子都知事は９月の都議会で、「持続可能な観光の発展には地域との調和が重要」と述べ、ポイ捨てを禁止する条例を制定する考えを示した。都は２８年度の施行を目指している。
読売新聞による９月の調査では、１１道県に罰則つきの条例があるが、徴収した実績はない。「専門の人員がいない」（北海道）のが主な理由という。都がモデル事例に位置づけるのが、６月から２０００円の過料徴収を始めた渋谷区だ。

title: トランプ氏支持率31% ロイター
body: Jason Lange[ワシントン　１９日　ロイター] - ロイター／イプソスの最新の世論調査で、トランプ米大統領の支持率が３１％と、２週間前から１％ポイント‌低下し、大統領１期目、２期目を通して最低水準となった。高騰するガ⁠ソリン価格に対する有権者の懸念が強まる中、１１月３日の中間選挙で共和党に厳しい審判が下される可能性が示された。「ジェネリ​ック・バロット（一般投票意向）」に関する項目の「きょう議会選挙が行われるとしたらどちらの党の候補に投‌票するか」との質問に対し、登録有権者の４７％が民主党、３５％が共和党と回答。民主党の１２％ポイントのリードは今回の選挙サイクルで最大となる。ジェ‌ネリック・バロット調査は、‌回答者がどちらの政党に連邦議会を主導し​てほしいと考えているかを測る全国調査。実際に上下両院の支配権を左右す‌る州別・選挙区別の選挙戦の詳細までは反映しておらず、共和党が制度的に優位な地域もある。２週間‌前のロイター／イプソス調査で​は、民主党が４４％、共和党が３７％で、民主党のリードは７％ポイン‌トだった。共和党の議会選候補への支持低下は、民主党に投票すると答えた女性の割⁠合が増えたことが主因だった。女性有権者の５０％が民主党に投票すると回答したのに対し、共和党候補への投票を考えているとの回答は３２％だった。男性も民主党を⁠支持する割合が共和党を上回ったが、その差は女​性より小さかった。ト‌ランプ氏の支持率は、２月に同盟国イスラエルとともにイランへの軍事攻撃を命じて以降、低迷している。戦争によってガソリン価格が急騰し、家⁠計が圧迫されている。トランプ氏の経済運営を支持しないと答⁠えた国民は６８％に上り、共和党支持者を自認する回答者でも３７％に達した。経済運営をより適⁠切に担える政党として、有権者の４０％が民主党を選び、共和党の３３％を上回った。調査は１９日まで４日間にわたり‌オンライ⁠ンで実施され、米国の成人１６７９人（うち登録有権者１２７９人）から回答を得た。​誤差は回答者全体でプラスマイナス２％ポイント、登録有権者でプラスマイナス３％ポイント。

title: トランプ氏 米露中会談に前向き
body: [ワシントン　１９日　ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は１９日、早ければ１１月にも中国の習近平国家主席、ロシアのプーチン大統領と軍備管理に関する首脳会談を行うことに前向きな姿‌勢を示した。実現すれば初の３者協議となり、トランプ氏にとって外交上の大きな賭⁠けとなる。トランプ氏は記者団に対し「核兵器と非核化について話し合うために会談が行われる可能性がある」とし、「習主席が開催を望むなら応じる。貿易など他の問題についても話し​合うことになるだろう」と語った。トランプ氏は中ロが接近する中、両国との冷え込んだ関係の改善を図ってきた。ただ、３者会談が開かれれば、首脳間の取引によって‌欧州やインド太平洋地域における米国の同盟関係が弱体化しかねないとして、警戒が広がる恐れもある。一方、３カ国の合意は世界的な緊張緩和につながる可能性もある。ロシアによるウクライナ‌での戦争が終結すれば、欧州の安全保障‌にとって過去数十年で最大の脅威が解消されることになり、軍備管​理で合意すれば、核兵器保有で３カ国に制約が課されることになる。関係者によると、ホワイトハウスは数週間にわたり、中‌国で１１月１８─１９日に開かれるアジア太平洋経済協力会議（ＡＰＥＣ）首脳会議に合わせ、非核化を中心議題とする３者首脳会談を開催する可能性を協議してきた。米紙ウォ‌ール・ストリート・ジャーナルは１８日、関​係者の話として、プーチン氏がその後、この会談を利用し、４年に及ぶウクライ‌ナ紛争の終結をロシアに有利な形で交渉することを提案したと報じた。提案は、ロシア産ディーゼル（軽油）燃料に関す⁠る合意に至った１０月９日のトランプ氏との電話会談で行われた。ロシア大統領府は１９日、首脳会談開催の可能性が協議で話題に上ったと明らかにした。ホワイトハウスはロイターのコメント要請に応じなかった。在米ロシア大使館と在米中国大使館も⁠回答しなかった。一方、ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は、トランプ氏が​プーチン氏と結んだディーゼル‌燃料に関する合意や、ロシアへの制裁を免除する大統領令を批判し、戦争を長引かせると警告している。トランプ氏は１９日、首脳会談の可能性について「応じるつもりだが、ウクライナのためというわけではない。⁠率直に言って、ロシアのウクライナを巡る対応には問題がなかったからだ」と述べた。⁠また「ゼレンスキー氏は事態改善にあまり役立っていない」とし、「別の誰かがウクライナを代表して交渉する時だ」⁠と語った。ただ、トランプ氏はこの日、北朝鮮の金正恩朝鮮労働党総書記との会談については、実現の可能性を控えめに語り、「‌彼とは非常⁠に良い関係にあるが、誰かが会談を求めているのかどうかは分からない」と述べた。トランプ​氏はこれまで、年内に金氏と会談する計画だと語っていたが、北朝鮮は核放棄の説得を目的とした協議には応じない姿勢を示している。

title: ウ軍 ドローンで空から負傷兵救出
body: ウクライナ軍は、前線で負傷した兵士をドローンで空から救出することに成功したと発表しました。こうした救出方法は、「世界初」だとしています。【写真で見る】ウクライナの戦場に「地上ロボット」 “無人で陣地制圧”も【任務に密着】ウクライナ軍の第92独立強襲旅団無人システム部隊は19日、他の部隊とともに前線で負傷した兵士1人を大型ドローンで空から救出したと発表しました。作戦が行われた詳しい日時や場所は明らかにしていません。現場では、ロシア軍のドローン攻撃が続いていたほか、周辺には地雷が埋まっていたため、地上を走る無人車両での救出は困難だったとしています。救出された負傷兵は現在、治療を受けていて、命に別状はないということです。第92独立強襲旅団は、空を飛ぶドローンによる前線からの負傷兵の救出は「世界初」だとしています。ウクライナでは、兵士を前線に送り込まずに救出する「無人システム」の開発が進められています。

title: 仏首相 一部に夜間外出禁止令要請
body: フランスのルコルニュ首相は19日、週末に各地で行われた生活費の高騰に抗議するデモで一部が暴徒化したことを受け、暴動や略奪を防ぐため、一部の地域で19日夜に夜間外出禁止令を発令するよう各知事に要請したと明らかにしました。【画像】【中継】生活費高騰…フランス各地で抗議デモ　一部“暴徒化”約2400人拘束　損害は数百億円規模か適用する範囲については関係する市長らと協議を行い、19日午後には公表できる見込みだとしています。これに先立ち、フランス大統領府は19日、週末の混乱を受け、ヌニェス内相が辞任を申し出たものの、マクロン大統領が拒否したと発表しました。マクロン大統領は、警察と治安部隊の指揮系統を維持するため、ヌニェス内相が留任すべきだと述べ、略奪を行った人への対処を早急に行うよう求めました。

title: 仏で抗議デモ 欧州各地に広がり
body:
フランスで先月中旬から続いている学生による抗議デモが今、大きく変化している。一部が暴徒化し、市庁舎へ放火するなど混乱が広がっている。【地図】ベルギー・ポルトガル・イタリアでも…各地で抗議デモ
火の手が急速に広がり、激しく燃え上がる鐘楼（しょうろう）。これはフランス中部、リモージュの市庁舎だ。19世紀に建てられた歴史的建造物がほぼ全焼する事態になった。原因は暴徒化したデモ参加者らによる放火だ。デモ参加者「バカ野郎マクロン!くそったれマクロン!」17日、物価高への抗議や教育環境の改善を掲げ、フランス全土でデモが行われた。当初、高校生らが始めたデモが今、様変わりしているという。デモ参加者（21）「今、最低限の食料品を買うだけでも100ユーロ（約1万8000円）は軽くかかる。一体どうやって生きていけばいいんだ?」デモ参加者（59）「不安なのは若者だけではないわ。私たちの声が届くまでこの状況があとどのくらい続くのでしょう」内務省によると、参加者はおよそ55万人に達したという。パリ市内の広場では、暴徒化した一部の参加者と治安部隊が衝突。デモ参加者が投石などを繰り返す中、治安部隊は催涙弾や放水で応戦。デモ参加者へ向けて一斉に突進する姿も見られた。
一方、デモに乗じた放火なども相次いだ。路上の車が、複数台まとめて炎上。燃え盛る車に、ごみ箱を投げつける人もいた。物を投げつけられているのは、警察車両。その場から逃れようと、猛スピードで走り抜けていく。さらに略奪行為も横行。スポーツ用品店の中にデモ参加者の一部が押し入ると、次々に商品を略奪し始めた。そこに駆けつけた治安部隊。1人を取り押さえたようだ。現地メディアによると、逮捕・拘束者の数はおよそ2400人に上り、警察官らおよそ1000人が負傷したという。
マクロン大統領は17日、デモに乗じた破壊行為について自身のSNSで「私たちの共和国に暴力の居場所はない」と非難した。番組は、ヨーロッパの政治に詳しい慶応義塾大学の鶴岡路人教授に話を聞いた。鶴岡教授は、ヨーロッパ各国はデモがさらに拡大しないかと神経をとがらせていると分析する。「今回のデモの対応を誤ると、来年の大統領選にも響くというのが、フランスでは非常に大きな問題。他の国でもいくつか選挙を控えている国があります。そういった国の現職の政府は自国でどのようなデモが起きるのか。他の国からのデモがどのように波及してくるのか。非常に戦々恐々として見ている」

title: 特定技能「給食」受け入れ再開へ
body: 外国人労働者の在留資格「特定技能1号」で外食業分野の新規受け入れが一時停止された問題で、政府は19日、医療・福祉施設などの給食調理員に限って飲食料品製造業分野に移管し、受け入れを再開する方針を有識者会議に示した。停止措置後に実施した調査で深刻な人手不足の実態が判明。別分野に付け替える緊急対応を迫られた形だが、識者からは受け入れ上限自体を引き上げるべきだとの声も上がる。【一覧】外国人材が集まらない業種は？給食調理員の新規受け入れを希望する事業者には、新たに申請を求める方向。年内に見直し方針を閣議決定し、来年4月の受け入れ再開を見込む。◇見直しにかじ切った政府会議では、厚生労働省が8月に医療・福祉施設の給食調理を請け負う38社を対象に実施したアンケート調査の結果を公表。回答した34社すべてで欠員が生じていた。うち4割は「多数が欠員」と回答。「撤退も検討している」との声もあった。政府は1月、特定技能1号の受け入れ上限を閣議決定したが、外食業は早々に上限の5万人を超える見込みとなり、4月に新規の申請受け付けを停止。5月の給食等調理員（学校給食を除く）の有効求人倍率は7・37倍に上っていた。このままでは患者や利用者の病態や治療方針に応じた給食の提供が困難となり、特に人手不足が深刻な地方で重大な支障を来すおそれがあるとして、政府は対応の見直しにかじを切った。◇「実態踏まえた上限数増加を」意見もただ、今回の再開は応急的な対応に過ぎない。移管先の飲食料品製造業も上限（13万3500人）に対して充足率が8割に迫る。9月の有識者会議では構成員から、今回の対応が与えた影響の検証や事業者への十分な周知の徹底、「実態を踏まえた受け入れ見込み（上限）数の増加」など踏み込んだ対応を求める意見が出ていた。【奥山はるな、宇多川はるか、横田愛】

title: ユニクロが値上げ 11商品を11月に
body:
カジュアル衣料品店「ユニクロ」は、原材料費の高騰や円安の影響を受け、秋冬商品を平均約４％値上げすると発表した。１１月１０日に１１商品を値上げする。【図解】一目でわかる…ファーストリテイリングの業績推移
「感動ジャケット」は税込み６９９０円から７９９０円に、「感動パンツ」は３９９０円から４９９０円になる。「カラーソックス」は４点９９０円だったまとめ買いを終了し、１点３９０円とする。１２月以降も値上げを実施する見通し。
９月には、「ウルトラストレッチレギンスパンツ」など一部商品のほか、ズボンの裾上げなどのサービス料金も引き上げている。

title: ユニクロ ソックス3点990円終了へ
body: ユニクロが16日、公式サイトにて、11月10日から一部商品とサービスについて、「平均販売価格の約4％アップ」の値上げを発表した。「感動ジャケット」6990円が7990円となる。【全身ショット】「オシャレで素敵」「かわちぃ」ユニクロのジャケットを使った内田理央の秋の私服コーデ「商品価格・サービス料金改定のお知らせ」と題し、値上げ対象となる商品の一覧を公開。値上げの理由については「原材料費や物流費の上昇、円安の影響が続く中、あらゆる工夫を重ねてまいりましたが、商品価格とサービス料金の一部を改定させていただくこととなりました」と説明。約4％アップという価格については、「継続して品質を維持し、お客様に長くご愛用いただける商品をお届けするため」とした。さらに同日より、「カラーソックス（50色ソックス）まとめ買い」「ソックスまとめ買い」の販売を終了とすることも発表。例えば「ソックスまとめ買い」3点990円だったのが、1点390円となる。なお同社は9月1日、送料やボトムスの補正料金、シャツ袖直しなどの料金について、値上げしたことも改めて発表した。■商品価格の改定（11月10日から）※価格はすべて税込【WOMEN】感動ジャケット¥6990→¥7990感動ジャケット/カスタムオーダー¥6990→¥7990感動スリムパンツ¥3990→¥4990PRINCESSE tam tam レーヨンプリントロングパンツ¥2990→¥3990【MEN】感動ジャケット¥6990→¥7990感動ジャケット/ライト¥6990→¥7990感動ジャケット/カスタムオーダー¥6990→¥7990UNIQLO and JW ANDERSON 感動ブレザー¥6990→¥7990感動パンツ¥3990→¥4990感動パンツ／ライト¥3990→¥499050色ソックス¥290→¥390

title: 個別指導トレーニング トラブル増
body: トレーナーから個別指導を受けるパーソナルトレーニングの契約トラブルが増加している。【写真】スポーツジムでトレーナーの指導を受ける人キャンペーン割引で契約し高額な解約料を請求されるケースもあり、国民生活センターはその場で判断せず、料金や解約条件などをよく確認するよう呼び掛けている。全国の消費生活センターへの相談は増加傾向にあり、2025年度は前年度から572件増の1457件に上った。年齢別では不明などを除き、20代以下が36．2％を占め最多だった。26年度は8月末時点で537件と、前年度を上回る水準で推移している。30代女性は体験参加で「1年分まとめて契約すると安くなる」と言われ、契約。仕事の都合で通えなくなり、解約を申し出ると「途中解約となるので割引適用がなくなり、通常料金で再計算して差額を請求することになる」と言われ、入会金も含め8万5000円の支払いを求められた。無料体験で2時間にわたり「この金額で入会できるのはきょうだけ」と勧誘されたり、サプリメントやエステなど関連サービスも勧められるまま契約してしまったりする事例もあった。国民生活センターによると、目標体形などのカウンセリングを踏まえてプランを提案されるため、断りにくさを感じ契約する例も見受けられた。解約手続きが複雑になりがちな点にも注意が必要という。同センターの担当者は、勧められた内容が自分の予算や通える頻度に照らし適切とは限らないと指摘。「いったん持ち帰って検討し、必要ない場合はきっぱり断ることが大切だ」と話している。

title: タイムズカーの画像巡る懸念 回答
body: パーク24は2026年10月16日、同社が運営するカーシェアリングサービス「タイムズカー」をめぐり、本人確認書類の画像保有期間についてのルールを見直したこと、現在同社が保有している本人確認書類の画像は10月末日までに削除することを発表した。不正アクセスによる個人情報漏洩を受けた対応だが、SNSでは、被害状況の確認や原因究明に支障が出るのではないかとする懸念や不安の声が上がっている。【画像】ルール見直しが決まった、本人確認書類画像の保有期間こうした懸念に対しパーク24は取材に、「被害状況の確認や今後の対応に支障が生じるものではないと考えております」と説明した。■「退会後7年間保有」から「登録完了後、即時削除」へパーク24は9月25日、外部からの不正アクセスによりタイムズカー会員の個人情報が漏洩した可能性があると発表。28日に、退会済みや入会未完了者を含む約660万件分のアカウントの氏名やメールアドレス、生年月日、住所などの情報が第三者に取得されたと発表。翌29日には、約160万件で運転免許証画像等の本人確認書類が漏洩したとした。パーク24は10月16日、本人確認書類の画像の保有や管理について、従来の「退会後7年間保有」から、「登録完了後、即時削除」にルールを見直したと発表した。従来は、本人確認書類の画像は、社内ルールにより保有不要となったもののほか、本人の請求に基づき削除していたという。このルールの見直しに伴い、同社が現在保有している本人確認書類の画像は、「ご本人様からのお申し出の有無にかかわらず、2026年10月末までに削除」するとした。この削除対応について、Xでは、漏洩が確認された本人確認書類の画像の画像を削除することで、被害状況の確認や今後の補償対応、原因究明に支障が出るのではないかとする懸念や心配の声が上がっている。例えば漏洩した本人確認書類画像の悪用が確認された場合の被害状況の確認や認定への影響を懸念し、「相当まずくないか？」「証拠隠滅では」などと疑う声も書き込まれた。

title: Curfew imposed in parts of central Paris and other cities after rioting across France
summary: It comes after the country's interior minister admits that police "lost control" in some cities.
body:
Are the riots in France a warning of an intense election to come?
French authorities have imposed overnight curfews in parts of central Paris and other cities after a weekend of riots and looting across the country.
Police in Paris said a curfew would be in force between 23:00 local time (21:00 GMT) and 06:00 in Place de la République, where protesters had gathered over the weekend, and the Les Halles shopping area.
A ban on unauthorised gatherings has also been imposed in several other parts of the city centre.
Partial curfews variously restricting the movement of young people and gatherings were announced for cities including Marseille, Bordeaux, Nice and Lyon in the south as well as Lille and other towns in the north.
Earlier Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez, who has been strongly criticised by opposition politicians over the preparedness for the disorder but whose resignation was rejected by President Emmanuel Macron, admitted police had "lost control" in some cities.
The protests began last month with students demanding better school conditions, but they have since escalated to take in a broader range of concerns, with numbers at demonstrations this weekend bolstered by trade unions and various protest groups.
More than 2,500 people have been arrested, officials said. One demonstrator's hand was blown off by a police crowd-control grenade, according to the AFP news agency. About 1,000 police officers were injured.
Following a crisis meeting on Monday, the prime minister said local mayors were being given the power to implement curfews "where they need", without specifying which cities where they would be enforced.
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu, who did not rule out imposing a state of emergency in the country, said the government would also set aside money to help affected areas recover from the damage, and the funding would be recovered from those behind the violence.
"There will be a law that will be put in place to find ways of making sure that those who have damaged properties will have to pay," Lecornu said.
He also announced a partial unemployment fund for those who could not work as a result of the riots and looting.
French police officers stop a vehicle entering the curfew zone in Lyon
Meanwhile, Nuñez said 200 investigators were analysing CCTV footage to try to identify possible ringleaders.
He attempted to resign on Sunday, but Macron refused "given the need for continued command of law enforcement", the Élysée Palace said.
The statement said Nuñez should be transparent over what Macron called "intelligence and foresight failings".
More than 2,000 shops and other businesses have been directly impacted by the weekend's violence, the head of France's Chambers of Commerce and Industry (CCI) says.
Its head Alain Di Crescenzo told France's broadcaster RTL that damage from the riots was estimated at "hundreds of millions of euros".
Jean-Luc Chauvin, the president of the CCI's Marseille branch, told the BBC that many of the city's shop owners were in "deep distress" and fear for their survival.
Looted goods have been listed on certain selling platforms, two French government ministers said. A Vinted spokesperson said the sale or solicitation of stolen goods was "strictly prohibited".
"Since this weekend, our teams have taken immediate action to identify and remove listings linked to the looting, and we have stepped up monitoring of suspicious listings," it said.
Vinted blocks French looters listing stolen goods for sale
'Very upsetting': Residents in shock after historic French town hall set alight
Some 550,000 demonstrators took to the streets over the weekend for protests against rising fuel prices, the cost of living and deteriorating public services, including schools.
Groups of rioters, some dressed in black and wearing masks and balaclavas, were seen setting fire to cars and buildings and looting businesses in Paris, Marseille and other cities and smaller towns.
In the central city of Limoges, the ornate 19th Century city hall was gutted by a fire started by rioters on Saturday, its clock tower and roof collapsing as the flames took hold.
The US Embassy in France has issued an alert advising its citizens to avoid areas affected by the recent demonstrations.
The warning says to "exercise caution" if they find themselves close to large gatherings. China and Germany have issued similar warnings.
Some politicians have accused the left-wing La France Insoumise party of playing a role in the violence, with Lecornu alleging in an earlier news conference that some groups "want to create chaos in our country up until the presidential elections".
The party's leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon, who will stand in next year's presidential election, responded by calling for the French PM to "prove his accusation" or "apologise, shut up, and stop stoking disorder".

title: Ukrainians dying because US restricting intelligence sharing, Zelensky adviser tells BBC
summary: Serhii Beskrestnov says there has not been enough time to warn people about incoming missile attacks. The White House said there had been no changes to intelligence sharing.
body:
Serhii Beskrestnov said "people have already died" due to lack of warnings about incoming missile attacks
Ukrainians have died because Kyiv is still not receiving reliable US warnings of incoming Russian attacks, according to a key adviser to President Volodymyr Zelensky.
Serhii "Flash" Beskrestnov told the BBC that lives had been lost because there had not been time to warn citizens about ballistic missile strikes, saying: "It's dangerous... I think it's really very bad... People [have] already died."
The adviser also said restrictions to Ukraine's use of the Starlink internet network were ongoing.
The White House said there had been no changes to intelligence sharing with Ukraine.
Ukraine first reportedan interruption to US intelligence sharing last week, as a row with the Trump administrations over its controversial deal to import Russian oil sent relations to new lows.
Despite the denials from Washington, many in Kyiv suspect the issues are not a coincidence.
On Monday morning, Zelensky wrote on social media: "Overnight two ballistic missile attacks were reported on the capital, one without warning, the second with only minimal time to take shelter."
Hours earlier, an interview the president did with NBC was published, in which he said intelligence sharing had been restored after a three-day pause.
"We are very thankful for this," he said. "Only [the] United States has this unique intelligence to tell our side when Russia uses ballistic missiles."
But Beskrestnov told the BBC that American intelligence continued to be incomplete and inconsistent, and that the US had failed to provide a clear explanation for the issue.
"This looks very strange," he said. "Sometimes we receive this information before the attack, another time we [do] not."
He continued: "And for example, last night we received it, but... one minute before the attack."
However, he said other collaboration with US continues, adding: "Intelligence data keeps flowing, and the issue is solely with the air raid alert component."
Beskrestnov also said the US had given no clarity about who was responsible for the ongoing restrictions to the Starlink internet network and its military service Starshield, which Kyiv uses to provide connectivity for drones, helicopters and military communications.
Last week, Starshield restricted the speed at which mobile units could move while staying connected to the network to 100mph (160km/h).
This has limited Ukraine's ability to shoot down incoming drones or to launch mid-range drone attacks into Russian-occupied areas.
Starlink owner Elon Musksaid last weekthat the US government ultimately controls access to Starshield, which was designed for the Pentagon, suggesting it may therefore be behind the restrictions. Trump has denied involvement.
Beskrestnov said he thought both issues occurring at the same time was "probably" a deliberate move to put pressure on Ukraine.
He told BBC News: "It's probably the United States trying to say [to] us, 'let's have the conversation, negotiation with Russia, you should find the compromise'."
Beskrestnov also said Ukraine had its own radar data to provide some limited warning of incoming attacks, but was urgently looking into using alternative communication systems.
He added: "Now we understand that something begins to happen with Starlink, and we're not sure what will be the next step.
"We understand that we should be prepared for some problems in future. And now we're thinking about an alternative for Starlink, not only for air defence, for communication between our forces, between our staff, for civilians also, because we don't know what we should expect in future regarding Starlink."
On Monday, when asked about intelligence sharing, Trump said: "We've given a lot to Ukraine. They've given us nothing."
Watch: Moment Ukrainian soldier lifted to safety by drone
Earlier, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio had said there had not been a "pause" to intelligence sharing.
"I don't know where [Zelensky is] getting these things or why he's saying these things to the press," he told reporters on Monday.
Rubio said he could not comment on the incident, adding: "I know a few nights ago there was a software problem involving their early warning system."
The BBC has contacted Starlink for a response.
A White House official said there were no changes to intelligence sharing operations between the US and Ukraine.
The official spoke on background to discuss intelligence matters. Trump is focused on ending the war, the official said, and added that the US has provided more aid to Ukraine than any other country.
Russian attacks continued late on Monday, with Ukrainian officials saying at least six people were killed - including a toddler in her pram and an 11-year-old girl - in a drone strike near a park café in the north-eastern Kharkiv region.
Zelensky described the attack in which another 14 people were injured as "absolute atrocity".

title: Kenya cult leader who told parents to starve children guilty of 191 murders
summary: Self-proclaimed pastor Paul Mackenzie was found guilty of 191 murder charges - all but one of them children.
body:
Paul Mackenzie's followers believed he was "Jesus's mouthpiece", the judge said
The leader of a Kenyan doomsday cult, Paul Mackenzie, has been found guilty of murdering 191 people, all but one of them children.
Mackenzie ordered members of his cult to starve their children to death so they could "meet Jesus".
His doctrine said that education was forbidden and modern medicine was "evil".
Twenty-eight other leaders of his cult were also convicted of murder. They had all pleaded not guilty, repeatedly insisting that nobody was forced to die.
Warning: This article contains details which some people might find distressing.
Delivering her eight-hour judgement in the port city of Mombasa, Justice Diana Mochache said Mackenzie's followers believed he was "Jesus's mouthpiece".
One of his co-accused said Mackenzie had told his followers that anyone who "resisted the directive to fast must be forced to go to heaven through kicks and blows".
Burials inside the forest where the cult was based were called "weddings". Those who died "were celebrated as having wedded with Jesus", the judge said.
One witness stated that a pregnant woman had been barred from nursing her new-born baby, who died 12 days later. "She was instructed to fast to death and follow her children," the witness said.
Mackenzie's former head of security, Enos Amanya Ngala, was initially accused but then entered a plea deal and became a witness for the prosecution.
Mackenzie and other leaders of the cult also face a raft of other legal cases, including for terrorism, radicalisation and denying education to children.
But this is the first time the pastor has faced a verdict on the most serious charges of murder. He is due to be sentenced on 6 November.
He was arrested in 2023, after the discovery of more than 400 bodies in shallow graves in Shakahola forest near the Kenyan coast, where Mackenzie had led his followers from across the country.
Stephen Mwiti, 48, said he lost all six of his children to the cult. His former wife was one of those convicted of murder alongside Mackenzie.
"I'm a happy man, that all persons have been convicted," he told the BBC outside court.
"All six of my children died in Shakahola forest," Mwiti said ahead of the verdict, visibly emotional holding a photograph of his family. "I only found and buried the remains of my son Samuel."
More than 400 bodies were dug up in Shakahola forest
Seventeen men were hired from the nearby town for the horrifying task of digging up the shallow graves. Some were paid just $8 (£6) a day.
"Every grave we found had at least three bodies," James, one of the gravediggers, told the BBC. "Some of the remains were of children as young as a few weeks old."
"We once found 12 bodies of children in a line inside a grave. It was massive, the bodies were arranged like clothes. One on top of another."
Gravediggers described some of the bodies of children as having had their "hands and legs tied and bodies wrapped in bedsheets".
Although many of Mackenzie's followers were from elsewhere in Kenya, some of the remains are of people who were familiar to the community because the people in the cult would often go to nearby Shakahola town for supplies and to fetch water from the River Galana which flows through the town.
"We would sometimes carry people on our motorbikes into the forest," said Salim Karisa, another gravedigger. "But it was so planned and secretive that nobody could tell what was happening inside."
Stephen Mwiti said he was happy with the verdict
Mackenzie established Good News International Ministries in 2003. Over the next 16 years, the church grew in popularity to draw thousands of followers in the church's branches across Kenya.
His church ran a television station called Times TV which would broadcast his sermons from his church in Malindi.
His End Days sermons included conspiracy theories that described education as "evil", healthcare as "against the doctrine" and digital identity cards as "the mark of the devil".
Mackenzie's son, Dan Paul Mackenzie, said he worked as a cameraperson in the church. "The children would sit at the back, adults in the middle, and everyone would sing worship songs all morning."
The self-proclaimed pastor would start his fiery sermons at noon, some of which included "casting out demons".
This is the building from where Mackenzie broadcast his sermons
The main church shut down in 2019 and Paul Mackenzie moved to Shakahola forest, encouraging his devotees to follow him.
Peter Shukrani, 23, says his mother relocated to Shakahola with him at the time. He started going to Mackenzie's church when he was eight years old and described him as his "spiritual father", adding that he would "never say a bad word about him".
When in the forest, Shukrani fell ill and his condition deteriorated because medication was banned.
"My mother would throw away all the medicine I was supposed to take because she believe that only God could heal me," Shukrani said.
The community was described as mud houses scattered across the vast forest. "We lived a quiet normal life, fasting for a few days then having a small meal," Shukrani said.
By March 2023 when the first remains were discovered by local herders, hundreds of people had died. "We would carry someone out of the forest but they were so frail that they would die in our arms," explained Salim Karisa, one of the gravediggers.
Shukrani was one of the men rescued from the forest.
He was ill and bed-ridden for weeks until that point, but his condition worsened because his mother would throw away all the medication he needed to recover.
"My mother believed Pastor Mackenzie's doctrine that medicine was evil," Shukrani said.
"I would have died if I wasn't rescued from Shakahola forest."
Peter Shukrani says he would have died if he had stayed in the forest but still believes Mackenzie is a good man
Many of the bodies are still unidentified owing to their advanced state of decomposition.
In the court documents, several are referred to as "unknown male child" and identified by the location of their grave and date of their discovery.
Despite the suffering endured by Mackenzie's followers, men, women and children who died due to starvation, strangulation and even being bludgeoned to death, as well as his own suffering, Shukrani believes Mackenzie was "a good person who cares for me".
"Mackenzie didn't force anyone to fast. People made those choices by themselves because of their beliefs," Shukrani said before the verdict was announced.
"I still love him and he is still my pastor."
In contrast Dan Mackenzie believed his father should be found guilty of murder.
"He was the leader, he was someone who they were looking [up to]. So he is a murderer of mass killing," also speaking before the verdict.

title: Tennis star Svitolina says emotional toll of Ukraine war led to Monfils separation
summary: The two top tennis pros married in 2021 and have one child together.
body:
Monfils and Svitolina played in the mixed doubles together at this year's US Open and reached the semi-finals
Ukrainian tennis star Elina Svitolina has announced the end of her marriage with French former tennis player Gaël Monfils, citing the emotional impact of the war in her country.
The 32-year-old, who is ranked number six in the world, wrote in a heartfelt post on Instagram about the effect the conflict and "what the war has done to me inside".
"This is the most difficult thing I have ever had to share," she wrote, saying "I need to find my way back to myself". Svitolina said she felt she could not do that within her marriage.
She said her husband Monfils, 40, "listened" and "respected what I need with a strength and grace I will never forget".
"Some battles happen deep inside you, and no amount of love from someone else can win them for you," the four-time Grand Slam semi-finalist wrote.
It was "the hardest thing I have ever had to tell the person I love", Svitolina said.
"Everyone knows how much Ukraine means to me," Svitolina, who grew up in Odesa, said.
Ukraine's Black Sea port city has been heavily bombed by Russia throughout the war.
Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
"What you didn't see were the sleepless nights, the doubts, and the feeling of slowly losing myself."
The tennis power couple married in 2021 and have one child together - a four-year-old daughter called Skai.
Svitolina said her daughter "will always come first", adding "our marriage is ending, but our family is not".
Monfils, a former world number six, was expected to play the final tournament of his career at next month's Paris Masters in an emotional farewell.
However, the two-time Grand Slam semi-finalist's retirement was effectively confirmed last week when he appeared on the International Tennis Integrity Authority's list of retired players.
Once a player removes themselves from anti-doping protocols, they are not eligible to compete in professional tournaments.
Monfils, who won 13 titles on the ATP Tour, is preparing to start a new career in finance after joining a Swiss wealth management firm.

title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world
summary: As the strongest El Niño on record continues to intensify, what impacts on weather patterns are already being felt across the globe? Sarah Keith-Lucas looks at the evidence.
body:
El Niño has been strengthening for several months now and is already having a significant impact on global weather patterns.
Countries including Indonesia, India and the United States have been experiencing droughts, floods and heatwaves in line with projections about how extreme weather events will be supercharged by the phenomenon.
The World Meteorological Agency says the record-breaking El Niño will strengthen further and persist until at least 2027.
Here are five ways its impact is already being felt around the world.
Several regions around the world are already experiencing anticipated El Niño impacts
Indonesia, which typically trends drier and hotter in El Niño years, is battling its worst wildfire season since 2015.
This year, since January, at least 895,657 hectares of land –nearly six times the size of Greater London– have been burned.
This is more than twice the area burned last year without the influence of El Niño.
The wildfires have led to school closures and an increase in hospital admissions across Indonesia.
Millions of people in Sumatra and Kalimantan have been exposed totoxic hazefrom the fires and around 175,000 people have suffered from respiratory illness.
More than 40,000 cases – which range from coughs to bronchitis and more serious conditions like pneumonia – involve toddlers.
In the eastern Pacific, where El Niño tends to strengthen hurricane activity, it has been a very active season so far.
There have been 22 named storms and 12 hurricanes, including 10 major hurricanes.
This is already above the number that would typically develop in the whole of an average season, with two months left to go until its end.
Here, El Niño provides the ingredients of higher ocean temperatures and weaker winds high in the atmosphere, making it easier for storms to gain strength.
Hurricane Polois one such example of this.
The hurricane experienced rapid intensification, producing wind gusts of 180 mph (285 kmh), fueled by the very warm waters produced by El Niño.
Polo was also one of three hurricanes churning away in the same basin at the same time, along with Odalys and Nolo.
Moreover, it has happened twice now in the space of a month.
Earlier in September, the energy produced by exceptional ocean heat resulted in three simultaneous hurricanes in the central and eastern Pacific: Lowell, Karina and Marie.
Until this year, the last time there had been three Pacific hurricanes at the same time was 2015.
In contrast, the Atlantic Ocean has remained eerily quiet.
El Nino has a tendency to increase wind shear in the north Atlantic, a factor which tears apart storms and limits formation.
There has only been one hurricane -Isaias- which made landfall in the Florida Panhandle and Alabama.
This was the latest forming hurricane on record in the satellite era (1960s onward).
Before this year, the record was 11 September, set in 2002 and 2013.
In an average season, there would have been 10 named storms, five hurricanes and two major hurricanes by this point.
This year, however, there have only been eight tropical storms: Arthur, Bertha, Cristobal, Dolly, Edouard, Fay, Gonzalo and Hanna.
The drier and warmer theme has also taken hold in India, where the essential monsoon rainfall has been 13% below average.
While the Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) would consider this still to be in the 'normal' range, the overall average doesn't reflect the variation in rainfall across India.
While Central India had around its normal expected rainfall, the east and north-east were around 26% drier than average and put into 'exceptional' drought. Southern states of India were 24% drier than average.
Even where rainfall was nearer to average, the rain did not fall continuously as is typical during the monsoon, instead flipping between long dry spells and extreme rainfall.
This adds more stress and vulnerability to agriculture yields.
India is influenced by a number of different weather patterns that can affect the monsoon season and so scientists suggest that El Niño may not have been the only factor.
Further west in the Pacific, it's also been an active season in eastern China and Japan as storms including Maysak and Dujuan have brought recent widespread floods and landslides.
According to the Japanese Meteorological Agency, there have been 10 tropical cyclones forming in the western Pacific Ocean - the highest number in a season since 1966.
During El Niño the warmer Pacific brings changes to wind patterns, meaning cyclones tend to form further east, away from Japan and east China.
However, this means there is a bigger distance and more time where storms can feed off the warmer waters, gaining energy to become more intense typhoons before they hit land.
Scientists believe that additional typhoons are likely to develop this year with the potential for further impacts to Japan or east China.

title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules
summary: Penalties are seen as too harsh on motorists who are penalised for parking on private land.
body:
Drivers will be given the right to challenge "rip off" private parking charges and more grace when using private providers under new rules set out by Andy Burnham.
The Prime Minister announced the changes after drivers repeatedly raised concerns penalties issued by private providers were too harsh and left motorists unfairly penalised.
In one case, a woman was taken to court in a £1,906 claim after taking longer thanfive minutes to pay at a car park in Derby. The charge waseventually dropped.
Private car parks already have an industry code of practice, but the RAC motoring group said the government's changes would protect drivers from the "poor practices of some private parking companies".
Burnham, the prime minister, said: "Being a few minutes late back to your car or typing one digit of your numberplate wrong shouldn't end with a hefty fine landing on your doormat.
"These charges leave people feeling ripped off and out of pocket, so I'm putting a stop to them."
The new rules will give drivers:
a guaranteed 5 minute period to decide whether to park
A 10 minute window to leave without facing a penalty
Cancellation of charges for issues drivers can't control, like vehicle breakdowns in car parks
Cancellation of charges for honest mistakes such as stopping to check directions, as well as for medical emergencies or broken ticket machines
Maximum charges of £20 on appeal for slip-ups like forgetting a parking permit, entering the wrong vehicle registration, or forgetting to confirm the registration in the machine when parking
A freeze on the maximum parking charge at £100, which is the same limit as the current private parking Code of Practice
Operators who do not comply risk losing access to DVLA data, making it far more difficult to pursue the car's owner even if they do issue a charge.
Private car parks are different to council-owned car parks and streets. RAC analysis of government data showed a record 17 million private parking tickets were issued in 2025/2026 - a 17% increase from a year earlier.
With each charge worth up to £100, the data, analysed by the Press Association and the RAC Foundation, suggests drivers could collectively face private parking charges worth more than £4.6m each day.
The yellow and black envelope of a Penalty Charge Notice, or PCN, is a dreaded sight for motorists returning to their car.
The AA has warned some drivers pay up even if they have done nothing wrong, just to avoid the hassle. It said people felt they would not get a fair hearing if they appealed fines, with many saying they feared legal action.
The current private parking industry Code of Practice, created by the British Parking Association and the International Parking Community, was introduced in 2024.
But the culture of motorists feeling they have been harshly penalised has spurred the government to present a formalised code to Parliament.
The British Parking Association told the BBC it welcomed the changes, but said "many of the principles within the new framework are already reflected in the existing voluntary Code of Practice".

title: 'I'm fed up of swiping': Why singles now want to meet IRL
summary: The BBC hears from people who think dating events are better value for money than dating apps.
body:
Olivia says she chose to attend this dating event because she has "app fatigue"
Checking in at a dating event in a bar in Guildford, Olivia Miller-Davis is understandably apprehensive.
Even bringing a friend with her doesn't remove the awkwardness at the start of the night.
"It's always nerve-wracking when you're meeting new people," the 28-year-old admits before downloading an app that will match her to other daters based on their star signs.
This is speed dating 2026-style and Olivia, like many people we speak to, is here because she's fed up of "endlessly swiping" or as some describe it "app fatigue".
She says she hates judging people with "really limited information and just a couple of pictures" because she doesn't feel she can "really fully commit" with so little to go on.
According to a recent study from online regulator Ofcom 11% of adults use dating sites but it suggests the time we spend on them is dropping, from a peak of almost four hours a month in 2023, down to three hours last year.
Edward believes apps are designed so you don't actually find "the one"
Olivia's first match on the night is Edward and he agrees that recent dating trends leave him feeling cold.
"I'm fed up with apps," he says.
"I mean, they're designed so that you don't find 'the one', because they want you to come back and use the app forever. They don't want you to get married from the app."
The event is organised by Love at First Sign, a dating company that uses an app to match people based on astrological connection, but most people are just using it as an icebreaker.
Director of events Lissy Cleminson says the way people date is changing and a big factor is more home working since Covid, which means people do not meet in offices or on the commute.
"The little meet-cutes don't happen so much when you're at home with your shirt up top and your pyjamas down bottom," she jokes.
As you may expect at a dating event many of the singles told us they were keen for that in-real-life or IRL experience.
There are a lot of #SingleTok and #Singlelife accounts on TikTok and Instagram reviewing dating events.
Candice Gallagher runs an account called @Candilicious and recently went to 10 different dating events in 10 weeks.
She describes herself as an entrepreneur and thinks in business terms dating events deliver "much greater return on investment".
The 40-year-old says all too often dating online can lead to "chat graveyards" with very limited conversation.
"At a dating event, everyone is single, everyone's ready to mingle, and your chances of having a good conversation are much greater."
Dating events provide a better "return on investment" than apps, says Candice Gallagher
Many people at the event in Guildford agreed dating events were better value for money because "you get to meet a range of people" in person for a similar cost to one date from an app.
These events typically cost around £15 to £30 and often include a drink and activity or icebreaking gimmick, in this case an app that is used throughout the night.
Olivia believes money plays a big factor in dating.
"I wasn't working for a bit because I changed careers and because of that I put dating on hold."
Olivia remembers thinking it "couldn't be a priority" and feeling she needed to wait until she was "earning enough" before dating again.
She is not alone in finding dating expensive.
More than a quarter of daters surveyed by Barclays suggested rising costs had changed how they date.
And a couple of recent studies suggest the monthly cost of dating - from apps to entertainment and clothes - can add up to around £130.
Many people at the event in Guildford agreed dating events were better value for money
Those running apps are quick to point out online is still a big part in the way people meet.
New research from Match Group, which owns Tinder and Hinge, suggests that out of those who had ever had a romantic relationship, about 21% of baby boomers surveyed met their most recent partner at a pub, bar or club.
Among Gen Z, it was just 4%.
The survey of 3,007 single people also suggests that of those who had ever had a relationship, 20% met their most recent partner on a dating app and 20% met through friends.
Chine Mmegwa, head of strategy, corporate development and operations at Match Group, said Tinder has made tweaks to its service in the past year to win back younger daters.
As well as helping users find out more about each other in advance of dates, through interactive music and astrology features, it has introduced "double date mode" for friends who want to date together.
And she said Tinder is doing more to encourage people to connect IRL. "They want to be in person. You've seen us launch events across the US and now the UK. We are bringing IRL experiences into the app.
"What we're doing is putting IRL into our experience. And so we are bringing that gap to what they're looking for in person, using the apps."
In Guildford, Olivia says her night was a success because she met some men she might want to go on a first date with.
When pushed by the BBC on whether she thought she had met "the one", she laughs and becomes understandably guarded.
"No, I'm not going to name anyone specific. But you'll be invited to the wedding if there is one!"

title: US bans DeepSeek AI from government use as tech tension with China continues
summary: DeepSeek is a powerful, popular and relatively inexpensive artificial intelligence model out of China.
body:
The US has ordered all artificial intelligence (AI) technology from the Chinese firm DeepSeek to be removed from most government systems.
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has banned all use of DeepSeek within civilian government agencies, and any technology built with the aid of its AI models.
As a powerful AI model that is open source - meaning it is free to access and less expensive to use - DeepSeek has beenseen as a disruptive forcein the ongoing AI technology race.
While the DHS notice did not detail the exact security concerns surrounding DeepSeek, the White House has this year criticised AI firms from China.
The DHS, DeepSeek, and the Chinese embassy in Washington DC have been contacted for comment.
The DHS made the order public on Monday, but the ban took effect from the end of July.
The order is specific to civilian agencies, including the Department of the Treasury, the Department of State and the Department of Justice. However, agencies within the Department of Defense are excluded.
The ban follows criticism of Chinese AI from the Trump administration, and from American firms.
White House tech lead Michael Kratsios wrote earlier this year in an internal memo that "malicious exploitation" of American AI firms had been occurring, mainly by rival firms in China.
Anthropic and OpenAI, both of which are poised to list on the public stock market in the coming months, have also claimed to have had their AI models essentially copied by some Chinese AI firms, including DeepSeek.
US president Donald Trump has made clear that he sees China as thekey US rivalwhen it comes to development of AI, something he sees as crucial to the future of the country.
DeepSeek has grown in popularity since itsinitial public releasein 2025, with models being in such demand that the company's servers have gone down at times.
While DeepSeek's free chatbot app is one of the most downloaded apps in the Apple App Store rankings, its AI models are also used by US tech companies. Companies like Snowflake, Vercel and OpenRouter all incorporate DeepSeek in their offerings to customers.
Startups have flocked to open source models like DeepSeek.
For a technology or AI developer, using DeepSeek in their work costs a fraction of what a closed model like Google's Google's Gemini, Anthropic's Claude or OpenAI's Codex would.
Similarly, the expense borne by DeepSeek to develop its models has been astronomically less than what it has cost US AI firms to develop their own.
Last year, DeepSeek said it took about $6m (£4.5m) to train the debut version of its model, while the costs associated with OpenAI's GPT-4 were roughly $100m. Such revelationssent tech stocks tumbling.
The most recent version of DeepSeek was released last week. Users of the model have praised it online, saying it beats even the most advanced AI tools out of OpenAI on common tasks for AI tools like computer software coding.

title: Ex-OpenAI worker accused of planting device had Saudi support, says court filing
summary: The Saudi government did not immediately respond to BBC requests for comment.
body:
A Saudi national charged with secretly planting a recording device in one of OpenAI's meeting rooms has been accused of having "considerable support" from the Saudi government, according toa court filing,externalin California.
US prosecutors claimed Abdulrahman Alfozan, who worked for the AI firm, was in "frequent communication... with a member of the Saudi royal family", and say a member of the country's military paid for a one-way flight to Saudi Arabia for his wife and son after his arrest.
The 35-year-old engineer was on Monday deemed a flight risk and denied bail, pending trial.
The Saudi government did not immediately respond to BBC requests for comment.
Alfozan had worked at OpenAI for around a year before he allegedly made his attempt to plant an audio recorder.
The AI company discovered the device, which was plugged into the back of a TV in a conference meeting room and covered up with toilet paper, on 30 September.
A camera was placed in the room and on 5 October, Alfozan was filmed entering and appearing to look behind the television where the audio recorder had been inserted.
He was arrested by the FBI on 9 October and his contract with OpenAI was terminated.
The court filing claimed the suspect's alleged conduct could pose "a danger to the national security of the United States", because executives from the tech firm met with government officials in the room during the days the device was believed to have been installed.
It said Alfozan's arrest came three days before he was scheduled to fly from San Francisco to Riyadh on a one-way itinerary with his wife and son.
Following the arrest, the document claims the defendant's wife told FBI agents who interviewed her that "her US visa was expiring" and so she and her son were "permanently moving back to Saudi Arabia", and her husband intended to do the same.
On 10 October, the day after Alfozan was arrested, his wife and son flew from San Francisco to Doha, Qatar. They travelled on a one-way business class ticket booked and paid for by a Saudi military official.
"Ultimately, the defendant has little incentive to remain in the United States to see this case through," the prosecutors argued.
US district judge Alex Tse on Monday denied Alfozan's attorneys request for his release on bail, saying "there is a risk of non-appearance that is significant".
The FBI investigation is ongoing.
Alfozan was scheduled to ‌appear ⁠in federal court in San Francisco later on Monday. If convicted, he faces a maximum penalty of five years in prison and a $250,000 (£188,000) fine.

title: Vinted blocks French looters listing stolen goods for sale
summary: The platform said since the weekend it had "taken immediate action to idenitify and remove listings linked to looting".
body:
Vinted says it has removed listings of items believed to have been looted from shops duringthe ongoing riots in France.
The second hand re-selling platform said following the weekend's disorder it had "taken immediate action to identify and remove listings linked to looting".
Shops across several French cities were broken into and ransacked during the outbreak of riots over the weekend.
"The sale of stolen goods, or soliciting them, is strictly prohibited on Vinted, and we have zero tolerance for it," a spokesperson for the company said.
Widespread looting was reported across Paris, Marseille and Lille, as well as other areas after protests against the cost of living and public spending turned into riots, leading to the arrests of at least 1,200 people.
More than 2,000 businesses were directly impacted by the weekend's violence, according to the head of the Chambers of Commerce and Industry (CCI).
Alain Di Crescenzo told France's broadcaster RTL that the riots led to hundreds of millions of euros worth of damage.
Groups of rioters, some wearing masks and balaclavas, were seen setting fire to cars and buildings as well as looting businesses.
Those that stole goods now appear to be looking to sell them on fast.
"Since this weekend, our teams have taken immediate action to identify and remove listings linked to the looting, and we have stepped up monitoring of suspicious listings," Vinted told the BBC.
"When our rules are breached, we act against the accounts involved, up to permanent bans."
The company said it was working with French authorities and the police, and was adapting its "processes to detect and counter emerging risks and malicious behaviour".
eBay has not noted any increase in listings linked to the looting in France, but said it works with law enforcement to investigate suspected stolen goods and takes appropriate action, including removing listings and taking action against sellers, when authorities confirm an item is stolen.

Reuters news agency reported luxury shops and boutiques were shuttered and surrounded by security guards at the Place Vendome in Paris.
But it said a host of stores in the French capital, including Dior, Rolex, Louis Vuitton and Ralph Lauren had their shopfronts damaged
In Marseille, football club Olympique de Marseille said its official store on the city's historic main avenue had been looted.
It has closed the store, along with fellow Ligue 1 club Lille, which said its club shop would remain closed until further notice.

title: Burnham vows end to 'rip-off parking charges' under new rules
summary: Penalties are seen as too harsh on motorists who are penalised for parking on private land.
body:
Drivers will be given the right to challenge "rip off" private parking charges and more grace when using private providers under new rules set out by Andy Burnham.
The Prime Minister announced the changes after drivers repeatedly raised concerns penalties issued by private providers were too harsh and left motorists unfairly penalised.
In one case, a woman was taken to court in a £1,906 claim after taking longer thanfive minutes to pay at a car park in Derby. The charge waseventually dropped.
Private car parks already have an industry code of practice, but the RAC motoring group said the government's changes would protect drivers from the "poor practices of some private parking companies".
Burnham, the prime minister, said: "Being a few minutes late back to your car or typing one digit of your numberplate wrong shouldn't end with a hefty fine landing on your doormat.
"These charges leave people feeling ripped off and out of pocket, so I'm putting a stop to them."
The new rules will give drivers:
a guaranteed 5 minute period to decide whether to park
A 10 minute window to leave without facing a penalty
Cancellation of charges for issues drivers can't control, like vehicle breakdowns in car parks
Cancellation of charges for honest mistakes such as stopping to check directions, as well as for medical emergencies or broken ticket machines
Maximum charges of £20 on appeal for slip-ups like forgetting a parking permit, entering the wrong vehicle registration, or forgetting to confirm the registration in the machine when parking
A freeze on the maximum parking charge at £100, which is the same limit as the current private parking Code of Practice
Operators who do not comply risk losing access to DVLA data, making it far more difficult to pursue the car's owner even if they do issue a charge.
Private car parks are different to council-owned car parks and streets. RAC analysis of government data showed a record 17 million private parking tickets were issued in 2025/2026 - a 17% increase from a year earlier.
With each charge worth up to £100, the data, analysed by the Press Association and the RAC Foundation, suggests drivers could collectively face private parking charges worth more than £4.6m each day.
The yellow and black envelope of a Penalty Charge Notice, or PCN, is a dreaded sight for motorists returning to their car.
The AA has warned some drivers pay up even if they have done nothing wrong, just to avoid the hassle. It said people felt they would not get a fair hearing if they appealed fines, with many saying they feared legal action.
The current private parking industry Code of Practice, created by the British Parking Association and the International Parking Community, was introduced in 2024.
But the culture of motorists feeling they have been harshly penalised has spurred the government to present a formalised code to Parliament.
The British Parking Association told the BBC it welcomed the changes, but said "many of the principles within the new framework are already reflected in the existing voluntary Code of Practice".
The new Code will apply in England, Scotland and Wales after motorists said they wanted independent oversight of the private parking industry.
Jack Cousens, head of roads policy at the AA, said drivers "finally have something which could offer them better protections against the worst private parking operators". He said in the past they have "aggressively attacked drivers to the point where many simply pay up".
But the RAC's head of policy Simon Williams said it wasn't the leap his firm had been campaigning for. He called for the banning of debt recovery fees being added on top of PCNs and said the current industry-run appeals bodies should be replaced by a single independent one.
The government said it will be consulting on the issue of debt recovery fees, as well as other recommendation from the Competition and Markets Authority.

title: PM says youth unemployment is a 'catastrophe and a moral failure'
summary: The UK faces "economic catastrophe" with one million young people not in work or training, the prime minister says.
body:
Britain needs to "invest in the success of our young people", Andy Burnham says
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has warned the UK faces an "economic catastrophe and moral failure" due to the nearly one million young people not in education, employment or training.
Writing in the Times newspaper,external, Burnham has laid out his case for the government to "invest in the success of our young people" rather than "pay for failure through the benefits system".
"Benefits will become the backstop, not the starting point," Burnham wrote in his piece published in Monday's paper.
This week, the government is expected to announce plans aimed at giving young people thousands of job opportunities. The Conservative Party has labelled the government's youth employment strategy "a disaster".
According to the latest data from the Office for National Statistics, there are almost a million people aged 16 to 24 known as Neets - not in education, employment or training.
Around 39% are unemployed while the remaining 61% are economically inactive, meaning they are not seeking work.
The number of 18 to 24-year-olds claiming unemployment-related benefits stands at 331,000, almost double the number in 2016, but lower than the peaks of around 500,000 seen after the financial crisis in 2008 and Covid in 2020.
The UK government will spend £353bn on welfare next year, just under half of which will go on the state pension; while the remainder is spent on benefits such as health, disability and unemployment payments.
In his opinion column, the prime minister said this reflected a "generation being denied its chance to get on in life".
"This is an economic catastrophe and a moral failure. And it must change," he wrote.
Burnham said two years of Covid lockdowns, social media that erodes "confidence and sense of belonging", an education system focused on the "university route", job markets with "too few opportunities" and failures of previous governments have all contributed to the Neets crisis.
"Today, the welfare system provides an assessment, a payment and, after that, goodbye," Burnham wrote. "Too often there is no support, no offer of skills and no opportunity to get a job."
He flagged a shift in the approach to welfare, which he said "will no longer begin by establishing which benefits a young person is entitled to" but rather "begin with their ambitions and the help they need to achieve them".
"We either invest in the success of our young people or pay for failure through the benefits system. We cannot afford to do both," Burnham wrote.
Ministers are this week set to release plans for 22,400 apprenticeships a year in businesses such as accountants, legal services and consultants, in addition to 40,000 placements in the construction industry.
The Conservative shadow business and trade secretary Julia Lopez said: "Labour have been a disaster for youth jobs. Their tax hikes and red tape have made it harder for businesses to hire, invest and grow, destroying opportunities for young people looking to take their first step on the career ladder."
The party has said they would cut £36bn a year from the welfare budget including by reintroducing the two-child limit for Universal Credit and restricting who receives housing benefit.
Green Party deputy co-leader Mothin Ali accused Labour of planning a "welfare cuts charter that would take support away from young people who are already struggling and vulnerable".
What does Neet stand for and why does the UK have so many?
Best thing we can offer young people is a job, not benefits, says chancellor
Burnham confirmed the long-awaited full review of young people and work will be published next month, and vowed to take its recommendations "seriously".
While the prime minister has emphasised the importance of incentivising young people into work, the review's author Alan Milburn suggested there could be cuts to benefits.
The former health secretarytold the Guardian,externalthat there was a need to "redistribute money from the welfare system to more employment support".
"This is not a workshy, snowflake generation," Milburn said. "If we provide more opportunities and we provide more support, the overwhelming majority of young people will take that, because that's what they want. The system isn't delivering what young people want, which is a job."
Milburn calculated that the government spends 25 times more on benefits for young people than getting them into work, describing thecurrent rate of Neets as "shameful".
In order to cut the benefit bill, both Burnham and Milburn will need to secure the support of those Labour MPs who previously baulked at Sir Keir Starmer's attempts to reduce spending by £5bn a year.
Backbenchers objected to proposals to tighten restrictions for those claiming working-age health-related benefits and, following a rebellion, the then-prime minister was forced to abandon his plans.
Two of Burnham's closest supporters Louise Haigh, his effective deputy, and Anneliese Midgley, his chief whip, who are now in government, were both leading lights in the welfare rebellion.
But difficult decisions are coming nonetheless and government insiders are clear that the link between cuts to welfare entitlement to fund increased jobs support is inevitable.
While Burnham has promised not to introduce "crude cuts", Labour advisers say it is impossible to leave the system for under 25s unchanged.
Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden is sympathetic to Milburn's call for a new, parallel benefits system for young people - but that level of change will require legislation.
Chancellor John Healey is due to give his first Budget on 28 October, and there is not expected to be much mention of welfare in it.
Instead a bill is being prepared and the New Year is when that is likely to be voted on by MPs.

title: Troubles legacy bill is not an amnesty for soldiers - NI secretary
summary: Amendments to the bill are being debated by MPs, as the long-awaited legislation returns to the House of Commons.
body:
The Troubles was a period of conflict which lasted for 30 years and cost the lives of more than 3,500 people
The secretary of state for Northern Ireland has rejected claims that planned changes to the government's Troubles legacy bill amount to an "amnesty" for former soldiers.
Sir Chris Bryant said it was "completely wrong" to suggest a requirement for theattorney general to consentto serious Troubles-related prosecutions was designed to pardon veterans.
The proposal is among a series of government amendments being debated by MPs on Monday after the long-awaited legislation returned to the House of Commons.
Speaking to BBC News NI, Bryant said it was a "sensible measure" to ensure there was "more consistency" in how decisions are made.
The legislation seeks to deal with the unresolved legacy of the decades-long violent conflict in Northern Ireland, which cost the lives of more than 3,500 people.
It was first introduced to Parliament last year following agreement on a joint framework with the Irish government.
NI Secretary defends planned changes to Troubles bill
Attorney general approval required for serious Troubles prosecutions
New legislation on Troubles legacy deal  introduced in Westminster
The government has said its amendments would "significantly reduce" the prospect of military veterans facing "rinse and repeat" investigations.
While some MPs have previously argued that planned protections for veterans do not go far enough, Sinn Féin has branded the amendments a "veterans' charter".
The Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) has also raised concerns that MPs will not have enough time to scrutinise the proposed changes.
Northern Ireland Secretary Chris Bryant said the bill will help Troubles victims' families
Sir Chris defended his plans for the attorney general to give consent to serious prosecutions, saying it was a recommendation in a recent Westminster human rights committee.
"We're not carving the Public Prosecution Service in Northern Ireland out of the process," he said.
"They're going to be working with the Crown Prosecution Service in England and Wales to make sure that they've got the same kind of rules and guidelines that apply to all of the prosecutions."
"The attorney general often exercises this kind of role. It's very different from their normal role, but it is something they do quite often."
Mark Thompson from the victims' group Relatives For Justice said he feared the bill could lead to unlawful killings being covered up by the state.
"Essentially, this impacts the victims of collusion and state violence," he told theBBC's Sunday Politics programme.
He accused the government of trying to take "control" away from local courts because it did not like some of the recent rulings in Troubles-era cases.
He pointed out that judges had ruled against the Army in "dozens" of inquests into killings carried out by soldiers, including those atBallymurphyandSpringhill.
Thompson argued that local courts had provided a "level playing field" but instead the government caved under pressure from the Army veterans' lobby in London.
"What they [the government] want to do is lift it out of a rule of law process and bring it to London and have a political decision."
However, lawyer Philip Barden, who has represented several ex-soldiers, claimed Army veterans were "put through the mill" in cases where there was "no evidence".
"What we want is an independent process so its not the PPS and the DPP deciding  in Northern Ireland who it is who should be prosecuted," Barden told the programme.
"We wanted a Supreme Court judge as being the most independent person that we could conceive of - not being a political appointment.
"The government have come up with the attorney general of the UK, who of course makes many decisions to prosecute people."
A spokesperson for the PPS said the organisation has "considerable experience in the prosecution of legacy cases".
"We will continue to approach our decision-making with complete impartiality and independence and in accordance with our Code for Prosecutors."
They added: "The proposed role for the Advocate General for Northern Ireland in relation to legacy prosecutions is a matter of government policy and ultimately for Parliament."
Conservative MP Sir Iain Duncan Smith (centre left) supported a veterans' protest in London last month
Barden defended the government's choice, saying if people disagreed with the UK attorney general's decisions they could always seek a judicial review, arguing that there was "complete independence".
He added that veterans' "primary cause of concern" was the number of repeat investigations into Troubles cases, despite a lack of any new or compelling evidence.
Natasha Butler's grandfather, Paddy Butler, was killed by the Army on theSpringhill estatein Belfast in July 1972.
She said she wants to "ensure victims and survivors are not lost in the politics surrounding this bill".
She added that "families have waited decades" for answers and the next generations "inherit the same silence".
David Crabbe served in the Ulster Defence Regiment and the Royal Irish Regiment during the Troubles from 1977 to 2007.
He feels "there has been too much politics at play in this" and called on the bill to be "victim-centred".
He added that "there has been a very narrow focus" on veterans.
Joe McVey says the the bill is "not perfect", but is keen to see it progressed
The commissioner for victims and survivors for Northern Ireland said legislation "needs to be truly victims centred".
Speaking onGood Morning Ulster, Joe McVey described the bill as "not perfect", but added "we're very keen that the bill is progressed" as it is "still a work in progress" and needs to be scrutinised in the House of Lords.
"When you look at the Troubles' Bill, we think there's an absence on a focus on victims and survivors and I think that's the message we keep trying to make very clear."
He added: "If we don't do it this time, then I think it'll be very difficult to predict when it's going to get a hearing again."
It seeks to replacethe previous Conservative government's contentious 2023 Legacy Act, which introduced a ban on inquests and civil actions related to Troubles-era incidents.
The act's most controversial element - offering immunity from prosecution to suspects who cooperated with an information recovery body - was disapplied after being found by the courts to be unlawful.
Labour's bill involves a legacy commission to investigate Troubles-related killings, a separate information recovery body, and a dedicated legacy unit within An Garda Síochána (Irish police).
The government said its amendments "significantly reduce" the prospect of military veterans facing "rinse and repeat" investigations.
The legislation will make clear the commission and coroners "must not regard the lawful conduct of members of the armed forces as equivalent to the actions of paramilitaries responsible for acts of terrorism"
The attorney general, currently Ellie Reeves, will be required to consent to all "serious" Troubles-related prosecutions
There would be measures to prevent "cold-calling" of veterans and extending provisions for remote attendance as part of the commission's work
Before any witness can be approached, the commission should consider if "compelling new evidence exists, or the likelihood of a witness being able to provide new information"
The commission must consider the "context and command orders" in which military veterans were operating
Former paramilitaries are barred from being appointed to the Victims and Survivors Advisory Group, and there is a requirement for at least one veteran or veterans' representative to be on the panel
There is a statutory review of the measures for veterans to ensure they "deliver as intended"
Opposition parties and backbench MPs have also tabled separate amendments aimed at changing the bill, but it is up to the Commons Speaker Sir Lindsay Hoyle to decide whether any of them will be accepted for debate.

title: First minister promises to look at Welsh council powers
summary: Plaid Cymru's leader makes pledge ahead of talks with Andy Burnham, who wants more devolution to councils.
body:
Rhun ap Iorwerth delivered a speech about devolution to Cardiff University on Monday evening
The Welsh government is to examine the powers councils have and how authorities work together regionally, the first minister has announced.
At a speech at Cardiff University, Rhun ap Iorwerth announced that this could lead to new legislation after the next election in 2030.
He is due to meet Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who says ministers in Cardiff should hand more powers to local authorities, later this month.
Ap Iorwerth denied offering a quid pro quo to the prime minister, who the Plaid Cymru leader is hoping will give the Cardiff government more powers and funding.
In the same speech, he also called on the UK government to stop duplicating the Welsh government's economic development work.
"Where power can sit as closely to the people it affects, it should," the first minister said at the event at Cardiff University's Glamorgan building.
"Whilst I am clear that we should never assume that what works for England will work for Wales, and vice versa - and I hope the prime minister acknowledges this – I know that our current arrangements aren't perfect either.
"I am convinced that, over time, Wales should move towards a more coherent and more streamlined system of local and regional governance.
"But that vision cannot be imposed."
Ap Iorwerth promised a green paper by the end of the term, followed by the "option" of new legislation from the next Welsh government.
He said he wanted to be in a "good position to reflect on what is working and where change is needed" by the end of the term, but said the "conversation" had to start before then.
The first minister said it would be a "detailed, meaningful exercise reflecting on where powers and specific competences should lie, how regional working works best and what effective cooperation looks like".
Rhun ap Iorwerth has previously written to the prime ministercalling for Wales to have the same powers as Scotland- including on railways, policing and justice.
Rhun ap Iorwerth is set to meet Andy Burnham at the end of the month
Asked by BBC Wales if he was trying to offer the prime minister a "quid pro quo", ap Iorwerth said: "I don't quite see it in that way.
"As somebody who wants power close to the people in Wales, I like the fact that the UK's new prime minister is talking that kind of language, but it means different things in Wales and England.
"The devolution programme that we're hearing from Andy Burnham is largely an England programme. What I want to do is find common ground with him."
The first minister questioned whether Downing Street's "devolution agenda" was "really an England-only agenda", and whether it came to a "shuddering halt at Offa's Dyke".
Economic development in Wales is devolved to the Welsh government.
But ap Iorwerth said Wales was living with a "confused" and "increasingly fragmented system".
"A succession of UK government programmes has been layered on top of devolved responsibilities and in some cases undermining them," he said.
"Some have funded worthwhile projects. Some have brought genuine benefits. But, taken together, they have made the landscape more complicated, more fragmented and more difficult to navigate."
He listed city and growth deals, and the former Conservative UK government's levelling up and shared prosperity fund projects, as examples.
"If powers have been devolved, central government should not continue to duplicate them," he said.
He called for a "practical agreement about how our two governments work together to unlock Wales' economic potential".
Asked later to clarify, he said he was not saying he wanted to get rid of city and growth deals - agreements between the UK government, Welsh government and local councils to help fund local projects - of which there are four in Wales.
"Whatever we have, lets look at what works well and how we can improve it," the first minister said.
